analysis.title: The Global Point, Wednesday, 04 November 2026
key_insights: Citi revises its 2027E DRAM supply/demand ratio to -3.8% from -8.7% and NAND to -3.3% from -6.1%, reflecting higher bit growth guidance from Samsung and Hynix and weak consumer NAND demand.
Citi still forecasts continued memory undersupply in 2027E. Server DRAM and eSSD demand growth is +53% and +52% YoY in 2027E, and the memory S/D fulfillment ratio is about 70%.

Korea's power transformer exports rose 76% YoY to US$514m in October, the highest monthly increment since at least Jan 2021. US$310m (+109% YoY) went to the US. Citi is positive on Korean transformer makers.
Korean exports of large high-voltage transformers (>10,000kva) rose 142% YoY to US$192m in October, with US$147m (+114% YoY) going to the US.
For 9M26 Korea's power transformer exports rose 7.0% YoY to US$4,004m, of which US$2,141m (+21.2% YoY) went to the US. Transformers above 10,000kva rose 30.8% YoY to US$1,358m in 10M26.

After meeting management and visiting Suzhou factories, Citi maintains Buy on Leader Drive. The company makes its own CNC control systems and rotary tables, which could lower equipment cost and insulate it from foreign equipment supply constraints.

Leader Drive plans to raise humanoid robot reducer shipments to about 50% of its reducer contribution in 2026 from about 20% in 2025. It plans to lift reducer capacity from 90k/month to 120k/month by end-2026 and 160k-180k/month by 2027.
Citi initiates Kelington Group at Buy with a TP of RM12.20, citing the wafer fab capex upcycle and UHP gas delivery expertise. It projects earnings growth of +33%/+50%/+25% for FY26E/27E/28E.
Citi's LatAm reform tracker shows only 16% of 63 reforms across 16 countries enacted, with over a third stalled or not yet filed. Slippage is concentrated in Colombia, Brazil, Panama and Uruguay.
Citi sees Colombia's Ley de Rescate as the most market-relevant LatAm catalyst over the next six weeks. Chile's corporate tax cut is the region's most investment-relevant reform win.
Citi upgrades Ferrovial to Buy from Neutral with a PT of EUR59.4. It estimates about 13% EPS CAGR over 2027-30 versus a 5% peer average, and about 13% equity IRR on the I-24 concession.

Ferrovial shares have underperformed SXOP by 5% since the I-24 award on 19 Aug, and market cap fell by about EUR8.7bn (about 22%) peak-to-trough. Citi opens a positive Catalyst Watch into I-285E commercial close in Dec-26.

Citi cut targets on several software and AI infrastructure names, including CoreWeave (to $128 from $159), Nebius (to $265 from $324) and DigitalOcean (to $160 from $190). Indonesian banks saw sharp cuts led by Bank Central Asia (to Rp6,500 from Rp9,800).

sector_views.rationale: Memory demand still outpaces incremental supply, with server DRAM and eSSD demand growing strongly in 2027E and the S/D fulfillment ratio at about 70%.
Record transformer exports in October, with a rising share going to the US.
Citi initiates Kelington at Buy on the wafer fab capex upcycle.
Ferrovial upgraded on undervalued concession assets and US P3 wins.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Highest monthly increment since at least Jan 2021, with US$310m going to the US.
Large transformers are most relevant to Korean power equipment makers under Citi's coverage.
Undersupply is easing on higher supplier bit growth guidance but persists.
Higher supply guidance and weak consumer NAND demand ease the deficit.
Delivery follows legislative arithmetic, with slippage in Colombia, Brazil, Panama and Uruguay.

trade_ideas.description: Positive Catalyst Watch on Ferrovial into I-285E commercial close (Dec-26).
trade_ideas.rationale: I-285E commercial close is a de-risking event, with I-24 financial close (Jul-27) and a possible I-77 South RFP adding momentum.

risk_factors: Where legislative arithmetic is missing, Latin America defaults to decrees, delays and dilution.
Higher memory supplier bit growth guidance and weak consumer NAND demand are easing the 2027E supply/demand deficit.
The Colombia budget cycle and Ley de Rescate over the next six weeks are the main test for LatAm reform delivery.
geopolitical: Six new Latin American governments and Lula's Brazil reelection attempt are trying to turn electoral mandates into legislation.
Minority governments in Latin America are relying on decrees, and IMF anchors in Bolivia, Honduras and Ecuador reliably move reform.
